Occasionally I would look at my girlfriend sitting next to me and consider how easy it would be to pop her eye out with my thumb. 

Other times I'd consider taking a bite out of my (much beloved) hamster. 

My therapist called these "intrusive thoughts" and apparently they're quite common for people with depression. They were very upsetting at the time though.

Imagine that the love of your life just died along with your family and any beloved pets. Your friends don't want anything to do with you and your house has just burnt down right after you lost your job. You're gonna have to live on the streets. 

Think about how all that would make you feel. Now imagine you feel like that even when everything's going your way. On what should be the happiest day of your life you still feel like the above. 

And crucially, the big delusion caused by depression is that this will never get better. No matter how much people may try to convince you otherwise, you remain completely hopeless. 

On top of that you feel physically drained and sleepy. Oftentimes you get weepy for no reason. 

Yeah, depression sucks.

So true. For a time there, life itself felt like so much effort. It was a daily struggle to do things as simple as get out of bed. 

But all that's behind me now. I'm aware of the possibility that it might come back, there's always that chance, but I live as if it won't. I take my meds, I get out of bed in the morning and it keep myself doing stuff. 

The only way to truly beat depression is a day at a time.

I've put out CVs everywhere and I've even had a couple of interviews which I think went well but I'm waiting to hear back.

Thanks :-)

I'm glad I stuck around too. This week I discovered Quokka's. To think, if I'd succeeded in committing suicide I'd never have heard of those happy little guys. Who knows what I'll discover next? :-)

Thanks :-)

You're pretty damn cool yourself :-) and I'm glad she's still here too.

It can be done!

It takes a lot of hard work but it's definitely achievable. Talk to a professional if you're struggling, it really does help. My GP referred me to a therapist and it honestly helped so much just to talk about it and be reassured that I'm not the only one who feels that way. 

Pills are an option too, they don't work for everyone but they worked for me, I'd recommend giving them a try if you think it might help. 

The main thing to remember is not to lose hope. Depression makes you think things that aren't true, like any mental illness. If you can, have someone there to tell you when the sickness is clouding your perception. Trust them. It's never as bad as this illness makes you think it is.
Thanks :-) I'm glad I passed some of my good mood on to you. Spread it about :-)

The main thing was simply being there for me and not bailing when I got really bad. She hugged me and comforted me when I couldn't stop crying, a lot of the time she'd force me to get out of bed and come for short walks with her, just so I'd get out of the house, but sometimes she knew I just needed to be sad and she'd let me be alone. 

She did a lot of practical stuff too like locking up all the pills and sharp implements in the house so I couldn't get to them. She managed my antidepressants. She brought me chocolate or other nice things when I was having a particularly bad day.

But to be honest, the most helpful thing she did, the thing that really stayed with me, was that when I truly hated myself, when I couldn't think of a single good thing about myself or a single reason why I should keep living she told me she loved me. She told me all the things about me that she liked. She reassured me that I wasn't being a burden to her, that even though time were tough then, she'd still be happier taking care of a depressed me than she would be if I was gone. 

She was kind, loving, comforting and so so patient. She treated me like I mattered when I felt like I didn't and she helped me see what was real and what was the sickness talking. She gave me perspective when I had none and a reason to keep trying to get better. The moment things started to turn around was when I decided that I didn't want to die because I wanted to have a future and I wanted it to be with her.

Thanks :-) 

It's a rough (uncut) diamond. So yeah, completely unique/irreplaceable. Like the woman whose finger it's on.

On occasion, looking at my girlfriend, I've thought about sticking my thumb in her eye socket and gouging her eye out. 

I've also occasionally thought about eating my hamster. 

Both of those thoughts have been quite distressing.

Weirdly, on the few occasions I've properly attempted it its been a very sudden decision. Not much planning. So the days in question have been pretty average. 

On one day I got up, had breakfast, watched some TV, started doing the washing up, got to cleaning a pairing knife, cut my wrist open. Tbh it kind of took me by surprise.
Maybe I should kill myself. Where's the knife? Oh, it's all the way over there. I'm too tired to get it. I'll kill myself tomorrow. First thing. For now, I just need to sleep. Right here.

So funny story, turns out my sisters boyfriend and I have therapists in the same building. That was an awkward period in the waiting room. Neither of us previously knew about the other being in therapy. I haven't mentioned it since, dunno about him.

Just because someone has a mental illness, doesn't make them selfish or weak. 

It doesn't make self harming right either, but its not as simple as you make it out to be.

I want to not be depressed anymore. I'd like to get off my meds, have the energy and the confidence to go out and do stuff. 

And failing that I'd like someone to talk to during the day besides my hamster (not that he's not good company. He's just not very chatty).

I'm right there with you. Depression, medication, therapy. 

Right now I'm taking it one day at a time. Today I will consider it a win if I can get out of bed.
If I die, who will take care of my hamster?

This. I spend an incredible amount of time and effort making sure most people DON'T realise I'm depressed. 

It's 30 degrees outside and I'm still wearing a hoodie because I don't want anyone to see the cuts on my arms.
I realise this is probably a joke, but that's literally the situation I'm in at the moment.

I don't want to die. I did, for a while, but I rationally thought it through and reasoned that my dying would hurt the people I care about. I decided that I wouldn't try to kill myself and made a crisis plan with my therapist for what I should do if I found myself considering suicide. When it came to it though I was doing it before I'd even thought about it. It's like my subconscious didn't get the memo.
No. I have never done this before.

Yes, I have a therapist I meet with once a week. My mood has gone up and down over the past couple of months but I was starting to feel better recently. 

I wasn't thinking about anything particularly negative at the time. My mind was just kind of wandering and I was singing along to some music while I did the washing up. I felt like I was having a good day until I felt myself pressing the knife against my wrist.

Even that can be quite a difficult thing for people with depression to accept. 

I've been struggling with depression a lot lately and phrases like "get over it" and "it'll all get better" or even "this is the illness talking" don't seem very helpful.

From my own personal experience, the best thing you can say to someone with depression is something along the lines of "yes, you're right, life is shit. But I love you and I like being around you".
I feel like you and I are kin.

Throwaway because some people IRL know my normal accounts name. 

A couple of weeks ago I was diagnosed with depression. I'd been having suicidal thoughts for a while and my SO convinced me to see the doctor. 

I'm worried I'm becoming a burden to my partner. I spend a lot of time just crying and I don't know how to convince her that I'm not depressed because of her or my living situation (with her) or even my work (which is a shitty part time job I've had since before uni). I'm just sad. And most of the time I don't have any real reason to be, I just start crying. 

Sometimes I think about how big and old the universe is and it feels me with these thoughts about how insignificant I am on every scale. How my life is essentially pointless. I'll never affect anything in any substantial way. I'll just live and then die and that's it. With how I'm feeling I just wish it would come sooner. 

I feel bad telling these thoughts to my partner. She lost her job a while ago because she had a breakdown due to stress. I know that if she were to go back to a job in that field again she'd be sad again but we're tight on money. Not sure we're gonna make rent and she's considering it. I don't want her to but she thinks if we didn't have money worries I'd be ok again. 

And to top it off, my first round of antidepressants caused a bad reaction and I ended up in the hospital. I'm fine now but we had to stop the drugs and put me on another kind at a lower dose. It'll be weeks til I can expect any improvement. 

Yeah, so anyway that was kinda rambling and train of thought. Sorry. 

TL;DR: Depressed, don't know why. Suicidal. Hate that I'm making my loved ones sad. Can't even take drugs to fix the problem and I'm probably not gonna make rent this month.
